annotations.title: Add rows to a Brilliant design

description: Use this when the user wants to change, restyle or add to a Brilliant design opened in this conversation, such as adding a section or a screen next to it, changing the copy or the colors, or making it darker. It takes the design's seed and Blueprint rows and applies them on that design's canvas: new rows add layers, and a row that leads with an id or #ref the design already has changes that layer. It returns how the rows applied, naming any row that did not apply. Its rows run up to 8,000 characters per call; a call of about 20 rows (about 1,500 characters), such as a page's frame and its first section, lands on the canvas within a few seconds. Rows take literal values (hex colors, numbers); design tokens are not available in this lane.

blueprint.description: Readable design rows, one element per line: its kind, text, size and colors in short form. Example: t("Sign in",Inter,15,b) f[(#FFFFFF)] is the bold white 15 px Inter text "Sign in". Children sit indented two spaces under their parent; no file() row; literal values (hex colors, numbers). Placeholder copy shows a person as a role label ("Account owner", "Home cook") rather than a first and last name: a profile, a name field's sample value and a testimonial's author alike. Brilliant applies rows as they arrive and the canvas animates each batch in, so a design reads best when its first rows set the frame and its main sections and later rows fill in the details.

seed.description: The slug of a design opened in this conversation (from the design result).
